reasoning_trace.step_0_visual_inspection: Figure 1: 'Measured EVM as a function of modulation index' confirms experimental evaluation of Comm performance. Figure 2: 'Simulated PSD' shows spectral broadening of CE-OFDM. No sensing results (range/doppler plots) are visible, only citations to [12, 13] for sensing properties.
reasoning_trace.step_1_concept_analysis: System: VLC using a Red Laser Diode (638 nm). Waveform: Constant Envelope OFDM (CE-OFDM). Coupling: 'Joint Waveform' (single waveform for both). ISAC Mechanism: The constant envelope allows high power efficiency in nonlinear LDs; the wideband/random-FM nature supports high-resolution ambiguity functions for sensing.
reasoning_trace.step_2_benchmark_verification: Comm: 250 MHz Bandwidth is significant for VLC. 2m link distance is typical for indoor desktop scale. 25 GSa/s sampling is very high, indicating offline processing (digital oscilloscope). EVM values (-29 dB) are good for 64QAM. Sensing: No physical benchmark (resolution/range) reported in this text; strictly theoretical argumentation.
reasoning_trace.step_3_strategic_critique: Contribution: Solves the PAPR/nonlinearity bottleneck of DCO-OFDM in O-ISAC. Gap: Experimental validation is limited to Comm (EVM); Sensing part is 'future work' or 'potential'. Trade-off: BW expansion (Eq. 3) reduces spectral efficiency compared to OFDM.

application.scenario_description: Indoor VLC link (2m) using Red Laser Diode, targeting simultaneous high-speed data and potential localization/material classification.

key_contribution.key_contribution: Experimental demonstration of CE-OFDM's superiority over standard OFDM in nonlinear VLC channels (EVM improvement) and theoretical framing for ISAC.
key_contribution.gap_addressed: PAPR and nonlinear distortion in optical ISAC transmitters (LEDs/LDs).
